propositions: Rebar's LLM runtime is currently Anthropic-shaped in practice despite being provider-agnostic in principle, with hardcoded provider name matching and capability gates preventing adoption of first-class Bedrock and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
The documented env vars REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL and REBAR_LLM_API_KEY are rejected at runtime by _pai_check_config despite being parsed by config.py, making the documentation false.

AWS Bedrock-hosted Claude is inaccessible as a first-class provider; PR #121's OpenAI-compatible gateway workaround silently loses prompt caching, retry/timeout, per-request timeouts, and native structured output.
Adopting pydantic-ai's provider_factory hook decouples provider selection from provider name string matching, enabling Bedrock and best-effort OpenAI-compatible backends through a unified seam.

The signed verdict sidecar must carry structured provenance (provider, model, endpoint host, tier, capabilities) rather than a model string alone, so consumers can distinguish first-class from best-effort verdicts.

Bedrock and direct-Anthropic paths must achieve equivalent retry and timeout guarantees through provider-native mechanisms (botocore.config.Config for Bedrock, httpx.AsyncTenacityTransport for Anthropic) rather than identical transport objects.
